items.title: Adani's Kutch Copper signs a three-year deal to buy recycled copper anode from Attero
items.summary: Attero will supply 2,000 tonnes of copper anode a month, recovered from discarded electronics and batteries, to Adani's Kutch Copper smelter in Mundra under a deal sources value at about $1 billion. Reuters reported the agreement was signed around three months ago and could trim the smelter's import dependence by around 5%.
items.why: A large, long-term offtake from a major smelter gives Indian e-waste and battery recyclers a domestic outlet for recovered copper and a benchmark for what recycled metal contracts can look like.

items.title: Cyclic Materials picks Schkopau, Germany, for its first European magnet recycling plant
items.summary: The North American rare earth recycler has secured a site near Leipzig for a plant with capacity similar to its Arizona facility, which can process up to 25,000 tonnes of scrap a year; launch is planned for 2028. It is the first of five scrap plants planned in the region to feed one central rare earth oxide separation hub.
items.why: Europe building scrap-to-oxide capacity outside China raises competition for end-of-life motors and hard drives, the same feedstock Indian magnet recyclers will need under the new magnet scheme.

items.title: China's black mass market splits: LFP quotes fall with lithium while ternary and LCO payables edge up
items.summary: Lithium carbonate slid to around 86,000 yuan a tonne by 26 November, dragging LFP black mass quotes lower, though deals fell by less as cost-supported processors held back. Ternary payables rose slightly as some hydrometallurgical plants paid up to fill long-term contracts, and LCO payables also climbed amid thin, contested trading.
items.why: Chinese payables set the benchmark that Indian recyclers and black mass buyers price against, and the gap between LFP and ternary material affects which battery scrap is worth collecting.

items.title: China's NdFeB scrap prices hold near highs, with Pr-Nd at 730-735 yuan/kg
items.summary: Recycled Pr-Nd from magnet scrap closed the week at 730-735 yuan/kg, with dysprosium at 1,240-1,260 yuan/kg and terbium at 5,600-5,800 yuan/kg. Prices rose early in the week alongside Pr-Nd oxide and then levelled off as recyclers bought only for immediate needs and sellers held stock back.
items.why: Magnet-scrap prices show what end-of-life motors and drives are worth, a key input for Indian e-waste recyclers weighing rare earth recovery.

items.title: Wayanad gathers about 103 tonnes of e-waste in a district-wide drive ahead of an e-waste-free declaration
items.summary: Kerala's Wayanad district collected 102.85 tonnes of electronic waste from homes, offices, institutions and government departments across all 23 grama panchayats and three municipalities. The material has gone to authorised agencies for processing, and the district is due to be formally declared e-waste-free.
items.why: It shows how panchayat-level collection with Haritha Karma Sena workers can pull household e-waste into the authorised channel that EPR recyclers depend on.

items.title: Dysprosium oxide export price climbs to $328/kg, past its February peak, as China supply stays tight
items.summary: Dysprosium oxide FOB China rose 1.5% in the week to $328/kg on 25 November, above the $327/kg high of 25 February, and terbium oxide rose 5.0% to $1,252/kg. Inside China, dysprosium oxide reached 1,610 yuan/kg on 26 November, up 14.2% since 23 October.
items.why: Rising heavy rare earth prices lift the value of magnet scrap and strengthen the case for India's planned magnet recycling and manufacturing capacity.

items.title: UK recycler Altilium signs LOI to supply recycled nickel MHP to Marubeni and POSCO HY Clean Metal
items.summary: Altilium signed a non-binding letter of intent to supply mixed hydroxide precipitate recovered from end-of-life EV batteries in the UK to Marubeni and POSCO HY Clean Metal. Its ACT3 plant under construction in Plymouth is designed to recycle 24,000 EV batteries a year and make about 5,200 tonnes of nickel MHP.
items.why: Offtake deals for intermediate products like MHP are a route Indian black mass processors could follow to reach Korean and Japanese cathode supply chains.

items.title: Fraunhofer ISI: Europe's announced battery recycling capacity now far outruns the scrap available to feed it
items.summary: Fraunhofer ISI puts Europe's current battery return volume at about 110–150 kt a year, rising to 240–320 kt by 2030 after cutting its earlier 2030 forecast of more than 400 kt by around one-third, while announced pretreatment capacity reaches just under 750 kt a year by 2030. Installed refining capacity is only around 200 kt a year against more than 800 kt announced, and black mass prices for some chemistries have fallen by over 50%.
items.why: A European feedstock glut and falling black mass prices shape the market Indian recyclers now serve at home after the black mass export ban, and show the risk of building capacity ahead of scrap supply.

items.title: Fortum produces its first battery-grade recycled nickel, cobalt and lithium samples for customers in Finland
items.summary: Fortum has sent customers samples of battery-grade cobalt sulfate, nickel sulfate and lithium hydroxide from a pilot campaign at its Harjavalta site, and is in offtake talks with potential buyers. The planned NEXT HYDROMET expansion would treat 3,000 tonnes of black mass a year, enough for about 138,000 EVs, with operations estimated to start in 2029 and €86.4 million of Business Finland support approved.
items.why: It shows European hydrometallurgy moving from black mass to sellable battery chemicals, the step Indian recyclers must now master at home after the black mass export ban.

items.title: Attero plans about ₹3,000 crore over five years to scale e-waste and battery recycling
items.summary: Attero CEO Nitin Gupta said the recycler will invest about INR 30 billion over five years, with roughly 40% going to lithium and nickel, and aims to lift annual e-waste capacity from about 225,000 tonnes to 1 million tonnes within four years. It also plans to grow lithium and battery recycling about five-fold, with new plants in Bengaluru (about 60,000 tonnes of e-waste a year) and Andhra Pradesh.
items.why: A capacity jump of this size from India's largest organised recycler would deepen competition for e-waste and battery feedstock and for EPR certificates.

items.title: BASF sells its battery recycling business, including the Schwarzheide black mass plant, to start-up Cylib
items.summary: Aachen-based Cylib is taking over BASF's European and North American battery recycling activities, including the Schwarzheide black mass plant that can handle up to 15,000 tonnes of batteries and scrap a year, at an undisclosed price. Closing is expected in the second or third quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approval.
items.why: A chemicals major exiting battery recycling shows how thin European margins have become, a signal for Indian recyclers weighing hydromet investment and export-linked strategies.

items.title: EU Commission weighs a levy on uncollected e-waste to raise about €15 billion a year for its budget
items.summary: The European Commission is considering a levy on waste electrical and electronic equipment that goes uncollected, as a new source of revenue for the EU budget. Dubbed an 'E-Waste-Tax', it is expected to raise roughly €15 billion a year.
items.why: A budget levy tied to collection shortfalls would push EU states to tighten WEEE take-back, which shapes the export markets and compliance models Indian producers and recyclers benchmark against.

items.title: China's LFP black mass eases with lithium carbonate near 91,000 yuan a tonne, while ternary payables hold
items.summary: Lithium carbonate traded sideways at around 91,000 yuan per tonne as of 19 November, and LFP black mass prices slipped slightly with it, though grinding plants resisted selling cheaply. Ternary black mass payables were broadly stable, LCO black mass tracked cobalt and lithium salts, and overall trading stayed thin as loss-making hydrometallurgy buyers held back.
items.why: Chinese black mass payables set the reference that Indian recyclers and pre-processors price against, especially now that India has barred black mass exports.

items.title: Myanmar supplies about 80% of China's October rare earth oxide imports as volumes rise 32% on year
items.summary: China imported 5,227 tonnes of unlisted rare earth oxides in October, up 4% from September and 32% from a year earlier, according to customs data compiled by SMM. Myanmar shipped 4,073 tonnes and Laos 1,037 tonnes, while mixed rare earth carbonate imports shrank to 50 tonnes, down 92% on year.
items.why: With China's oxide feed resting on two neighbouring suppliers, any disruption there flows into Pr-Nd and magnet-scrap prices that set the economics of magnet recycling in India.

items.title: Coal India-led consortium gets an LoI for a 1,200-tonne rare earth magnet plant under the ₹7,280 crore scheme
items.summary: The Ministry of Heavy Industries issued a Letter of Intent dated 19 November to a consortium of Coal India and NFTDC, declared the L2 bidder, for a sintered rare earth magnet facility with 1,200 tonnes of annual capacity over a seven-year term (two years of pre-construction, five of operation). The scheme, approved in November 2025 with a ₹7,280 crore outlay, aims for 6,000 tonnes a year of domestic magnet capacity and drew 20 bids.
items.why: New domestic magnet makers will need neodymium and dysprosium feed, giving Indian recyclers that recover rare earths from magnet scrap and e-waste a potential home market.

items.title: Korea Zinc and Solarcycle merge US recycling arms into a new platform, Jupiter
items.summary: Korea Zinc will hold a majority stake in Jupiter, which combines its PedalPoint Recycling unit with US solar panel recycler Solarcycle across eight certified facilities and one million square feet of processing space. Recovered metals will be refined through Korea Zinc's plants, including its planned US$7.4 billion Project Crucible smelter in Tennessee, due to start production in 2029.
items.why: It shows a major smelter buying into panel collection to lock in recycled silver and copper, a model Indian recyclers and module makers may need as MNRE drafts solar recycling rules.

items.title: Germany's disruptive-innovation agency SPRIND takes a stake in battery recycler Cylib
items.summary: SPRIND is investing an undisclosed amount in Cylib, whose water-based process recovers lithium from black mass with stated recovery rates of over 90% for lithium, graphite, nickel, cobalt and manganese. Cylib is building a hydrometallurgical plant in Dormagen, an EU Critical Raw Materials Act strategic project, and since September has run a black mass line at Wernberg-Köblitz designed for up to 10,000 tonnes a year.
items.why: State equity in lithium-from-black-mass refining in Europe sets a benchmark for the hydrometallurgical capacity India now needs after banning black mass exports.

items.title: Technology Development Board backs Hyderabad's NeoSeekermetals to recover critical minerals from e-waste and battery scrap
items.summary: The DST's Technology Development Board signed an agreement to fund a ₹20 crore project, with ₹10 crore approved from the government's RDI Fund as optionally convertible debt. NeoSeekermetals will use it to take its patented process for extracting critical minerals from e-waste and lithium-ion battery waste from TRL-5 to TRL-9.
items.why: Government money going into an indigenous recovery process matters for Indian recyclers now that black mass must be processed at home.

items.title: China's Pr-Nd oxide hits a monthly high as magnet-scrap prices climb with it
items.summary: SMM's weekly review puts Pr-Nd oxide at 725,000–727,000 yuan/mt after an early-week dip to 715,000–718,000, while dysprosium oxide sits at 1.56–1.57 million yuan/mt and terbium oxide at 6.45–6.5 million. NdFeB scrap was quoted at 720–730 yuan/kg for Pr-Nd content, 1,230–1,250 yuan/kg for Dy and 5,600–5,800 yuan/kg for Tb.
items.why: Scrap payables track oxide prices closely, so firmer Pr-Nd and Dy lift the value of magnets recovered from Indian e-waste and motors.

items.title: Smelters pour money into e-scrap capacity, but the fight for feedstock has yet to heat up
items.summary: Aurubis's Georgia smelter is built for about 180,000 tonnes a year, Atlantic Copper's new CirCular plant for about 60,000 tonnes, and Umicore has committed €450 million to expand Hoboken refining by 2030. Yet Boliden's Rönnskär took in 18,257 tonnes of electronics and alloy feed in Q3, down 1.8% year on year, and the 2026 copper concentrate benchmark treatment charge fell to zero.
items.why: With copper concentrate scarce and global smelters adding e-scrap lines, demand for Indian PCB and copper-bearing scrap could firm over the next few years.

items.title: India's battery recyclers face a purity test as black mass must meet battery-grade specs
items.summary: Indian black mass typically holds about 35% nickel and cobalt by weight against a Chinese benchmark of over 40%, PwC India says, while the critical mineral recycling scheme sets indicative purity benchmarks of at least 99% for lithium, nickel and cobalt salts. Producers of EV and portable batteries must use recycled material equal to at least 5% of a battery's dry weight in FY28, rising to 20% from FY31.
items.why: With black mass exports now prohibited, recyclers' returns depend on refining it to grades that cell makers and the incentive scheme will accept.

items.title: China's commerce ministry and eight other departments issue guidelines to build out recycling networks, including EV batteries
items.summary: Released on 17 November, the guidelines cover collection and dismantling of retired traction batteries, solar modules and wind turbine blades, and call for joint scrapping of electric vehicles with their batteries and a study of digital IDs for traction batteries. China aims to have a recycling system with full collection networks by 2030, with makers encouraged to run collection systems matched to their sales.
items.why: Tighter collection rules in China shape global black mass and battery scrap flows, and offer a template as India builds its own battery EPR system.

items.title: Two UK battery recycling projects using University of Leicester technology win £5.4 million
items.summary: The £3.7 million STOCKMAN project will develop a hydrometallurgical route to recover lithium, nickel, cobalt and graphite, while the £1.7 million RECLAIM project, led by Ecoshred and Lithium Battery Recyclers, will trial direct recycling. Both are backed by the Battery Innovation Programme delivered by Innovate UK.
items.why: Direct-recycling and graphite-recovery methods being funded abroad are options Indian recyclers can watch as they look to move beyond black mass.

items.title: North Carolina bans lithium-ion batteries from landfills and most incinerators from 1 December
items.summary: North Carolina's ban on sending lithium-ion batteries to landfills and most permitted incinerators starts on 1 December, pushing local programmes to take loose batteries and battery-containing devices at drop-off points. The state, which holds more than 80% of US lithium ore reserves in two counties, is also asking residents to keep batteries and electronics out of kerbside recycling bins.
items.why: Disposal bans are a proven way to raise collection volumes, a lesson India's battery EPR system can use as it tries to pull spent cells away from the informal sector.

items.title: US recycler SPR takes a fifth plant in California, lifting its capacity towards 6.5 million panels a year
items.summary: Solar Panel Recycling has taken over a 42,000-square-foot site in Porterville, California, which will start at 1 million panels a year once retrofitted, with processing hoped for by February. With four other sites in North Carolina, Texas and Georgia, the company says its total capacity will reach 6.5 million panels a year and that it recovers at least 95% of the aluminium, glass and silver.
items.why: It shows the plant scale and recovery rates solar recyclers are reaching abroad, a benchmark for India as MNRE drafts module recycling guidelines.

items.title: Ex-China Pr-Nd oxide rises $4/kg in a week as dysprosium and terbium firm in Rotterdam
items.summary: SMM's weekly ex-China assessment puts Pr-Nd oxide at $113–125/kg FOB, up $4/kg, with Pr-Nd alloy also up $4/kg at $130–144/kg FOB. In Rotterdam bonded warehouses, dysprosium oxide gained $50/kg to $3,400–4,200/kg and terbium oxide $100/kg to $7,500–8,300/kg.
items.why: Firmer prices outside China lift the value of the neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium locked in scrap magnets, improving the case for Indian magnet-recycling projects.

items.title: CPCB orders state inspections of over 2,000 recyclers, 309 of them e-waste units, to catch fake EPR claims
items.summary: A July order from the CPCB chairman, reported by Reuters, asked all states to inspect more than 2,000 recyclers, including 309 e-waste processors, checking machinery, plant trial runs and electricity use against claimed output. Units found with forged or manipulated paperwork can be blocked from generating EPR certificates, and Uttar Pradesh, home to about a third of e-waste recyclers, has lined up 33 of them for immediate audits.
items.why: Producers buying EPR certificates face a higher risk that credits from weak recyclers get blocked, which should favour verified, high-capacity recyclers.

items.title: Australia cancels the tender for its $24.7 million national solar panel recycling pilot
items.summary: Australia's environment department scrapped the procurement for the pilot without awarding a contract, after months of suspension over a complaint; the scheme was meant to collect up to 250,000 panels from up to 100 sites over 12 to 18 months. The minister has asked for urgent advice on next steps and says the government remains committed to a national pilot.
items.why: It shows how slowly solar-waste take-back schemes can get off the ground, a useful caution as India's MNRE drafts its own module recycling guidelines.

items.title: US magnet recycler REEcycle clears an SEC hurdle for its planned Nasdaq listing via a SPAC
items.summary: The SEC has declared effective the registration statement for REEcycle's merger with Hall Chadwick Acquisition Corp., a deal that values the Oklahoma rare-earth magnet recycler at about US$350 million plus a US$50 million earnout. Shareholders vote on 10 December, and REEcycle's first commercial plant is planned at roughly 160 tonnes a year of processing capacity.
items.why: A public listing for a magnet-to-oxide recycler gives Indian investors and recyclers a live valuation benchmark for rare-earth recovery from end-of-life magnets.
items.source: Hall Chadwick Acquisition Corp. via GlobeNewswire

items.title: South Korea plans regulatory exemptions to recycle more cathode and anode scrap from battery plants
items.summary: At a 12 November meeting in Daejeon, South Korea's environment ministry said it will designate circular-economy zones with regulatory exemptions by the end of 2026 and back recycling trials through its regulatory sandbox in the first quarter of 2027. Companies asked for wider circular-resource eligibility so that production scrap now classed as waste faces lighter storage and transport rules.
items.why: With black mass exports now banned, Indian recyclers and cell makers will be watching how Korea frees up gigafactory scrap from waste rules, a model India's own battery-waste regime may need.

items.title: Korean firms commit 650 billion won to rare-earth magnet plants ahead of US defence sourcing curbs
items.summary: LS Cable & System will spend 350 billion won ($263 million) on a magnet plant in Gumi with more than 1,000 tonnes a year of capacity from 2028, while KMMI plans 300 billion won through 2030 for a 6,000-tonne plant in Pohang. The push comes before US rules from 1 January 2027 restrict China-sourced magnets across the whole defence supply chain.
items.why: Non-Chinese magnet capacity is growing fast in Asia, which raises demand for traceable rare-earth feed, including recycled material that Indian magnet and e-waste recyclers could supply.

items.title: Veolia opens a French hydrometallurgical plant able to process nearly 7,000 tonnes of black mass a year
items.summary: Veolia said on 12 November it has started a battery-metals recycling facility in France's Grand Est region that can treat nearly 7,000 tonnes of black mass a year, roughly 20,000 tonnes of batteries, recovering over 90% of the cobalt, nickel and copper. Feedstock will come from France, the UK and Switzerland, and Veolia expects close to 700,000 tonnes of batteries to reach recycling in Europe within five years.
items.why: More refining capacity in Europe adds buyers for black mass just as India has banned its export, so Indian recyclers will be competing with hubs like this for feedstock and offtake partners rather than selling to them.

items.title: China's magnet-scrap prices hold at highs as dysprosium oxide climbs past 1.5 million yuan a tonne
items.summary: SMM's weekly review puts Pr-Nd recovered from NdFeB scrap at 715–720 yuan/kg, recycled dysprosium at 1,230–1,250 yuan/kg and recycled terbium at 5,600–5,800 yuan/kg after successive gains. Dysprosium oxide rose sharply to 1.51–1.52 million yuan/mt and Pr-Nd oxide to 715,000–718,000 yuan/mt as of 12 November.
items.why: Firm heavy rare earth prices improve the economics of recovering magnets from Indian e-waste and motors, a segment the critical-mineral recycling scheme is meant to build up.

items.title: COSMO AM&T and Carbon Resources plan a ₹40 billion LFP cathode plant in Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh's cabinet on 10 November approved a ₹40 billion plan by South Korea's COSMO AM&T and India's Carbon Resources for a battery materials plant at Naidupeta in Tirupati district. The first phase, targeted for mid-2028, would make 30,000 tonnes a year each of iron phosphate precursor and LFP cathode material, rising to 180,000 tonnes each (360,000 tonnes combined) by 2031.
items.why: A large domestic LFP cathode maker would be a natural local buyer for lithium recovered by Indian recyclers, which matters more now that black mass can no longer be exported.

items.title: India bans exports of lithium-ion battery black mass with immediate effect
items.summary: A DGFT notification moves battery waste and scrap under ITC (HS) code 85491400 from 'Free' to 'Prohibited' until further orders, covering unsorted scrap free of lead, cadmium and mercury, which the notice identifies as lithium-ion black mass. The change is limited to that category and is not a blanket ban on all battery material.
items.why: Indian shredders that sold black mass abroad must now find domestic refiners, which should shift payables and favour recyclers with their own hydrometallurgy capacity.

items.title: LS MnM opens an Ulsan battery materials plant that can take black mass as well as MHP
items.summary: The South Korean smelter completed the plant at its Onsan site on 10 November, with nickel sulfate capacity equal to 24,000 tonnes of contained nickel a year. It will also make cobalt sulfate, manganese sulfate and lithium hydroxide for precursor makers.
items.why: More Korean refining capacity that accepts black mass adds to the buyers Asian recyclers can sell to, a market Indian exporters are now shut out of.

items.title: Germany's Tozero makes first delivery of recycled lithium carbonate under a long-term contract
items.summary: Tozero shipped lithium carbonate from its Gendorf demonstration plant, sized for about 500 tonnes of battery waste a year, to ceramic-colour maker Botz under a binding supply deal. The startup aims to recover over 80% of the lithium in used batteries and sells mainly to construction, ceramics and lubricant buyers for now.
items.why: It shows small black-mass refiners can earn early revenue from non-battery lithium buyers while working towards battery grade, a path open to Indian start-ups too.

items.title: Ecoprogetti's automated solar panel recycling line is running in northern Italy
items.summary: Ecoprogetti has supplied a fully automated module recycling line to a site in Sale, Italy, run by Raee.man, a subsidiary of Haiki+. The line can handle up to 120 panels an hour and has reported 94% uptime since it began operating in early 2025.
items.why: Indian module makers and recyclers preparing for MNRE's coming solar recycling guidelines can use this as a benchmark for what a commercial automated line delivers.

items.title: China's black mass payables fell through October, with LCO dropping hardest
items.summary: SMM says the lithium payable for LCO black mass slid from above 70% to about 63% in October, while ternary black mass cobalt payables fell from 73.46% to 68.9% and lithium payables to 70.02%. The cuts followed a month in which lithium carbonate fell more than 20% and cobalt sulfate over 25%.
items.why: Lower Chinese payables set the benchmark Indian black mass sellers are quoted against, squeezing margins for recyclers that sell rather than refine.

items.title: Rivian widens Redwood Materials deal to cover scrap, end-of-life packs and second-life storage
items.summary: Redwood Materials will recycle Rivian's production scrap and retired EV batteries collected through Rivian's service centres, deciding pack by pack whether to reuse or recycle. An earlier April 2026 deal is already deploying 10 MWh of storage built from repurposed Rivian packs at its Normal, Illinois plant, and Redwood says it recovers over 95% of lithium, nickel, cobalt and copper.
items.why: It shows the full-lifecycle OEM–recycler contract that Indian EV makers may need to meet battery EPR targets, combining reuse and recycling under one partner.
